items: Back pain after a small bump

caption:
Koko had been taking it easy, worried about fragile bones. But bone is living tissue, and it adapts to the load you give it.

Current guidelines suggest regular resistance and weight-bearing exercise, built up gradually, supports bone health. Clinical Pilates can be one useful piece: reformer springs let you add resistance in small steps, and standing work trains balance and leg strength too.

Pair it with walking and stairs across the week. If you've been told you have low bone density, let us know so moves can be chosen to suit you, and keep your GP in the loop. Our Pilates team at Hybrid Physio can get you started. Book online via the link in bio.

General information only — not a substitute for an individual assessment.
